synthesis.evidence_balance: mixed — a bounded, self-funding, high-margin franchise offset by a permanent >10%-revenue customer loss, one-directional cuts, and a declining FY27 base.

bull_points.claim: The de-rating is discrete and event-driven — three dated gap-downs tied to Q4 earnings, the Avis termination notice, and a CEO change — not a slow secular bleed, so the shock is identifiable rather than diffuse.
bull_points.source_ref: EDGAR 8-K item codes at the gap-down dates (not blanket-labelled earnings)

bull_points.claim: Absolute EBITDA rose across the multi-year window (229→304→306→342→362) even as the margin % drifted from 42% to 37%, so the falling-margin optic overstates deterioration when read against the rising dollar base.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement (margin % + absolute EBITDA reconciler)

bull_points.claim: The company is self-funding — LTM levered FCF is positive at $53.9M and FY26 guides FCF of $140–$150M — so survival does not depend on capital-markets access.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Cash Flow 'Levered Free Cash Flow' [LTM 12 months Mar-31-2026]

bull_points.claim: Interest coverage of 5.6x and no near-term maturity wall (earliest debt is the 2028 Term Loan) mean the leverage is serviceable rather than a refinancing cliff.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense [LTM 12 months Mar-31-2026]

bull_points.claim: Post-shock guidance was cross-source verified against the primary 8-K release (revenue $985–$995M) and the delivery track-record shows actual ≥ guided floor on EBITDA 8/10 and EPS 3/3, with FY25 MET — the revised guide is credible, not aspirational.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Guidance (latest guide + sign-aware delivery track-record)

bull_points.claim: Management is returning capital through buybacks, retiring 7.7% of shares over ~1.7 years (164.7M→151.9M), signalling balance-sheet confidence rather than distress.

On a forward-adjusted basis the stock trades at ~4.3x EV/adj-EBITDA and ~3.5x adj-P/E, with the TEV/LTM EBITDA multiple sitting at the 0th percentile of its own 19-quarter history — a compressed own-history read, not just a peer read.

On the fundamental_deltas the name carries a far higher EBITDA margin (37% vs peer-median 18%) and higher 1y revenue growth (10% vs 8%) — posing whether the deep peer discount is RESIDUAL (overshoot) rather than fully EARNED, though the peer set is heterogeneous.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Operating Statistics (name vs peer median: growth/margin/leverage/beta)

bull_points.claim: Government Solutions — 47% of revenue — is described as long-term recurring contracts (e.g. the $998M 5-year NYC DOT contract) with ~$71M trailing-12m bookings, an annuity leg unaffected by the Avis loss.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript(s): Verra Mobility Corporation, Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 06, 2026.rtf; Verra Mobility Corporation, Q4 2025 Earnings Call, Feb 24, 2026.rtf

bear_points.claim: Avis Budget — a customer representing over 10% of total revenue — issued a contract termination notice, and management sizes the annualized hit at $135–$145M of revenue and $120–$125M of segment profit, a genuine and permanent loss of a material revenue block.

Consensus is cutting hard and in one direction — FY26 revisions run 0↑/8↓ and GAAP EPS 1↑/5↓ last month, and the current-FY consensus path fell -16% on EBITDA and -29% on GAAP net income from the 12m-ago mark — this is the REAL forward signal, not an optical trailing artefact.

bear_points.claim: Consensus LT growth was slashed from ~9.5% toward 1.9% (one broker to -11.2%), so the long-run compounding thesis the high margin implies has itself been repudiated by the estimate cut — the discount may be EARNED, not residual.

bear_points.claim: FY27 consensus EBITDA of $333M sits BELOW FY25's $362M and FY26E's $382M, i.e. the base case is now year-over-year EBITDA decline, not a temporary dip — a value-trap-shaped trajectory.

twin_reference_cases.distinguishing_fact: Recurring-contract software/services name that gapped down on a guide cut and management change, then re-rated as bookings visibility held.

decisive_question.question: Is the Avis loss plus the LT-growth downgrade a one-time reset around a still-growing recurring-contract core (overshoot), or the first leg of a structurally contracting earnings base (value trap)?

evidence_for.claim: Management sizes the Avis hit at a bounded $135–$145M annualized and reaffirms mid-single-digit Commercial Services and recurring Government Solutions growth, framing it as a discrete removable block.
Absolute EBITDA had been rising through FY25 ($362M) and Government Solutions carries a $998M 5-year NYC contract plus ~$71M trailing bookings, an annuity leg independent of Avis.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ transcript(s): Verra Mobility Corporation, Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 06, 2026.rtf; Verra Mobility Corporation, Q4 2025 Earnings Call, Feb 24, 2026.rtf

evidence_against.claim: FY27 consensus EBITDA of $333M falls below both FY26E and FY25 actual, and consensus LT growth was cut toward ~1.9%, implying the market now models a contracting rather than dipping base.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (FY26/FY27 consensus EBITDA, latest snapshot)

evidence_against.claim: FY26 revenue and EPS revisions are one-directional (0↑/8↓ revenue; 1↑/5↓ EPS) with the current-FY EBITDA path down -16%, signalling the analyst base sees ongoing erosion, not a one-time reset.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (current-FY consensus path; ragged, absent lookbacks n/a)

key_unknowns: Whether the >10%-of-revenue Avis relationship is fully lost or partially retained under a successor arrangement — the transcript describes ongoing 'constructive' negotiations before the termination notice, leaving the final revenue impact unresolved.
Whether the interim CEO becomes permanent and what strategic direction follows — leadership is unsettled (Jonathan Keyser appointed interim) at a critical juncture.

Covenant terms are UNKNOWN (extraction failed) and the covenant basis is not disclosed — an opaque leverage constraint that could bind if EBITDA continues falling; treat as a downside risk, not a neutral gap.

The peer set is HETEROGENEOUS (market caps $430M–$15.9B, 37x span) so every peer multiple is a confidence-gated input, not a clean benchmark — the earned-vs-residual split cannot be cleanly read off the peer median.
The export date is unverified (a floor ≥ 2026-06-09) so the very latest estimate and price movement may post-date the snapshot.
No 5y P/E percentile context is clean because the trailing EPS is one-time-distorted — the own-history cheapness signal rests on the distorted basis.
Whether the fwd-adjusted ~2.6x net-debt/adj-EBITDA holds if FY27 EBITDA prints near the $333M consensus rather than the FY26 guide.

caveats: RESOLVED (P/E basis) — trailing GAAP P/E 5.1x is one-time-distorted: latest GAAP EPS 0.85 is ~3.1× the recent median 0.28, so 5.1x is not a meaningful 'cheap' read. Clean read: forward adjusted guide $1.19–$1.25 → ~3.5x at the current price; CIQ P/LTM 16.8x uses a different (lower) trailing EPS basis.

EV/EBITDA stale-price caveat — CIQ's Financials→Multiples current TEV/LTM 8.5x is priced at its last Close 2026-03-31, 97d before the 2026-07-06 reference; for a since-re-rated name this 'current' multiple AND the own-history range/percentile built on it are stale. The Comparable-Analysis sheet reads 4.7x on a current price — prefer that figure and re-pull the Financials multiple.
